record.paper_title: A New Paradigm for Scattering Theory of Linear and Nonlinear Waves: Review and Open Problems
record.original_question: In very long-range N-body scattering, when two-body interaction terms decay like |x|^-µ with µ ≤ √3 - 1 and standard proofs of asymptotic completeness break down, can one prove asymptotic completeness and determine whether new scattering channels with self-similar weakly localized solutions are required?

evidence.quote: In the study of N-body scattering, it is observed that if the two-body interaction terms vanish as |x|− µ , where µ ≤ √ 3 − 1, the proofs of Asymptotic Completeness (AC) break down. This occurs because the asymptotic dynamics of some channels are governed by time-dependent potentials, resulting in a self-similar spreading part due to the concentration of the solution at zero frequency over time. The community generally believes that AC holds in these cases but lacks a formal proof. Based on the analysis outlined here, it is conceivable that in the very long-range case, new scattering channels may emerge, featuring self-similar weakly localized solutions.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the quantum N-body Hamiltonian on $L^2(\mathbb{R}^{3N})$ (or, after removal of the center of mass, on $L^2(\mathbb{R}^{3(N-1)})$),
$$H = \sum_{i=1}^{N} -\frac{1}{2m_i}\Delta_{x_i} + \sum_{1\le i<j\le N} V_{ij}(x_i - x_j),$$
where the pair potentials $V_{ij}: \mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}$ are smooth and satisfy the very long-range decay condition
$$|\partial^\alpha V_{ij}(x)| \le C_\alpha (1+|x|)^{-\mu - |\alpha|}$$
for some exponent $\mu$ with $0 < \mu \le \sqrt{3} - 1$.

Define asymptotic completeness (AC) in the usual sense: for every state $\psi$ in the continuous spectral subspace of $H$, $e^{-itH}\psi$ decomposes as $t \to +\infty$ (and as $t \to -\infty$) into a sum of asymptotic channels indexed by cluster decompositions $\mathcal{C}$ of $\{1,\dots,N\}$, with each cluster moving along a modified free trajectory and its internal state being a bound state of the corresponding subsystem Hamiltonian (with possibly Dollard-type or Graf-type time-dependent modifiers in the free evolution).

(a) Prove or disprove that $H$ is asymptotically complete under the above very long-range assumption $\mu \le \sqrt{3}-1$.

(b) Determine whether, in addition to the standard cluster channels, new scattering channels are required—specifically, channels supported on self-similar, weakly localized profiles arising from the concentration of the wave at zero frequency under the time-dependent effective potential—and, if so, give an explicit description of these channels and incorporate them into a complete asymptotic decomposition.
artifact.status_search_result: Asymptotic completeness for N-body Schrödinger operators is established for short-range potentials and for long-range potentials with decay exponent $\mu > \sqrt{3}-1$ (results of Sigal–Soffer, Dereziński, and others), but the very long-range regime $\mu \le \sqrt{3}-1$ remains unresolved. Existing proofs break down because the asymptotic dynamics are governed by time-dependent effective potentials producing self-similar zero-frequency spreading, and no complete proof has appeared in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Asymptotic completeness of N-particle long-range scattering (Sigal-Soffer)
status_evidence.snippet: Asymptotic completeness for N-body long-range scattering established for sufficiently slow decay above the threshold.
status_evidence.claim: AC is known for long-range pair potentials with decay exponent above sqrt(3)-1, not below.

status_evidence.title: Stationary scattering theory, the N-body long-range case
status_evidence.snippet: Within the Dereziński-Enss class of pair potentials, asymptotic completeness is known and the N-body scattering matrix is well-defined at non-threshold energies.
status_evidence.claim: Current results cover the Dereziński-Enss long-range class but not the very long-range regime.
